The residue of $21$ modulo $5$ is the integer $0\le r<5$ such that

$$
21≡r\,(\text{mod}\,5).
$$

**Method 1**

To find the residue $r,$ we need to write $21$ as an integer multiple of $5,$ plus the residue $r.$

We note that $21≡1\,(\text{mod}\,5)$ because

$$
21=4\cdot 5+1.
$$

Therefore, the residue of $21$ modulo $5$ is $1.$

**Method 2**

We can use the subtraction property:

$$
\begin{aligned}21 & ≡21-0 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡21-4\cdot 5 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡21-20 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the residue of $21$ modulo $5$ is $1.$
